- Overestimate early in the forecast horizon, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast values.
- Underestimate when true values rise sharply after a dip; adjust upward for sudden rebounds.
- Overshoot in the final 5–10 days of forecast; cap or smooth out late-period peaks.
- Model tends to overreact to recent high values; apply mean reversion bias toward prior 10-day average.
- Forecast often lags true values by 1–3 days; shift forecast slightly ahead by 1–2 days for better alignment.
- Avoid overfitting to recent volatility; dampen forecast sensitivity to short-term noise.
- When true values exceed forecast by >5% for 3+ consecutive days, reduce next forecast by 2–3% to avoid runaway bias.
